summary: Sung Yong Kang is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at Seoul National University and the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Seoul National University (attested 2008 and 2022) and the University of Vienna.

Sungdoo Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg (2001) under Lambert Schmithausen, served as Director at Geumgang University, and became a professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).
Sungtaek Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Stony Brook University and at Korea University, where he was Director (attested 2012-2013).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli.

Suniti Kumar Chatterji was an Indologist and linguist educated at Calcutta, London, and Paris under Jules Bloch. He taught at Calcutta (1914-1952) and served as National Professor in Humanities (c. 1965-1977) and President of the Asiatic Society (c. 1953-1955).

Surama Dasgupta was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied under Surendranath Dasgupta, earned degrees from the University of Calcutta, and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge in 1948. She served as Reader at the University of Lucknow.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Tribhuvan University under the supervision of Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Calcutta and Cambridge under McTaggart and Ward. He held posts at Chittagong College, Cambridge, Presidency College, Sanskrit College (Principal, c. 1931-1942), and the University of Calcutta.
Surendranath Majumdar Sastri was an Indologist and historian who studied under traditional teacher Hara Prasad Sastri. He served as a Reader at Patna University (attested 1924).

Surya Kanta was an Indologist and linguist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Frederick William Thomas in 1937. He served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of the Punjab (attested 1939).

Surya Kumar Bhuyan was an Indian historian and Indologist. He earned degrees from Presidency, Calcutta, and a PhD from SOAS (1936). He served as Principal of Cotton University (1918) and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (c. 1957-1960).
Suryanarayana Shukla was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied at Rajgopal Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya under Nandakishore Pandey, Ramanujacharya, and Shridatta Pandey.
Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University, studying under doctoral supervisor Ch%00n-fang Y%08 and instructors including Bernard Faure.
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2004, having studied under Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, and others.
Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr. (attested 2009).
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She was a professor at Ohio State University from around 1970 to 2011.

Susan Naquin is a historian and Sinologist. She earned her BA at Stanford and MA and PhD at Yale. She was a faculty member at the University of Pennsylvania (1977-1993) and professor at Princeton University (1993-2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard (PhD 1986) and Free University of Berlin. She taught at Yale (1989-1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996-2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum (2000-2026).
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who held a post at Amherst College beginning around 1978.

Susan Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Central Asian studies, and Sinology who earned her PhD at SOAS (1995). She directed the International Dunhuang Project (1993-2017) and is a professor at the Sainsbury Institute.
